find-skills.name: find-skills
find-skills.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

skill-creator.name: skill-creator
skill-creator.description: Guide for creating effective skills. This skill should be used when users want to create a new skill (or update an existing skill) that extends Claude's capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, or tool integrations.

skill-installer.name: skill-installer
skill-installer.description: A tool to install skills from remote git repositories directly into .trae/skills directory. Supports subdirectories for monorepo skill collections.

skill-auditor.name: skill-auditor
skill-auditor.description: A standard compliance checking tool for Trae skills. Use this skill when you need to verify if a skill follows best practices, specifically checking for dependency completeness, proper file encoding, path consistency, cross-platform compatibility, internationalization support and correct packaging structure.

agent-skills.name: agent-skills
agent-skills.description: Collection of agent skills for React, React Native, and web development. Includes composition patterns, best practices, and design guidelines.

sp-brainstorming.name: sp-brainstorming
sp-brainstorming.description: You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, or modifying behavior. Explores user intent, requirements and design before implementation.

sp-dispatching-parallel-agents.name: sp-dispatching-parallel-agents
sp-dispatching-parallel-agents.description: Use when facing 2+ independent tasks that can be worked on without shared state or sequential dependencies

sp-executing-plans.name: sp-executing-plans
sp-executing-plans.description: Use when you have a written implementation plan to execute in a separate session with review checkpoints

sp-finishing-a-development-branch.name: sp-finishing-a-development-branch
sp-finishing-a-development-branch.description: Use when implementation is complete, all tests pass, and you need to decide how to integrate work - guides completion of development work by presenting structured options for merge, PR, or cleanup

image-generation.name: image-generation
image-generation.description: Converts Markdown documents to high-quality images (PNG/JPG) using Python and headless browser rendering. Ideal for creating social media posts, documentation screenshots, and sharing rich text content as images.

obsidian-skills.name: obsidian-skills
obsidian-skills.description: Collection of Obsidian-specific skills for note management, markdown editing, canvas creation, and database operations.

pdf-generation.name: pdf-generation
pdf-generation.description: Professional PDF generation from markdown using Pandoc with Eisvogel template and EB Garamond fonts. Use when converting markdown to PDF, creating white papers, research documents, marketing materials, or technical documentation. Supports both English and Russian documents with professional typography and color-coded themes. Mobile-optimized layout (6x9) by default for Telegram bot context, desktop/print layout (A4) for other contexts.

planning-with-files.name: planning-with-files
planning-with-files.description: Implements Manus-style file-based planning for complex tasks. Creates task_plan.md, findings.md and progress.md. Use when starting complex multi-step tasks, research projects, or any task requiring >5 tool calls. Now with automatic session recovery after /clear.

powershell-windows.name: powershell-windows
powershell-windows.description: PowerShell Windows patterns. Critical pitfalls, operator syntax, error handling.

sp-receiving-code-review.name: sp-receiving-code-review
sp-receiving-code-review.description: Use when receiving code review feedback, before implementing suggestions, especially if feedback seems unclear or technically questionable - requires technical rigor and verification, not performative agreement or blind implementation

sp-requesting-code-review.name: sp-requesting-code-review
sp-requesting-code-review.description: Use when completing tasks, implementing major features, or before merging to verify work meets requirements

sp-subagent-driven-development.name: sp-subagent-driven-development
sp-subagent-driven-development.description: Use when executing implementation plans with independent tasks in current session

sp-systematic-debugging.name: sp-systematic-debugging
sp-systematic-debugging.description: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes

sp-test-driven-development.name: sp-test-driven-development
sp-test-driven-development.description: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code

ui-ux-pro-max.name: ui-ux-pro-max
ui-ux-pro-max.description: UI/UX design intelligence. 50 styles, 21 palettes, 50 font pairings, 20 charts, 9 stacks (React, Next.js, Vue, Svelte, SwiftUI, React Native, Flutter, Tailwind, shadcn/ui). Actions: plan, build, create, design, implement, review, fix, improve, optimize, enhance, refactor, check UI/UX code. Projects: website, landing page, dashboard, admin panel, e-commerce, SaaS, portfolio, blog, mobile app, .html, .tsx, .vue, .svelte. Elements: button, modal, navbar, sidebar, card, table, form, chart. Styles: glassmorphism, claymorphism, minimalism, brutalism, neumorphism, bento grid, dark mode, responsive, skeuomorphism, flat design. Topics: color palette, accessibility, animation, layout, typography, font pairing, spacing, hover, shadow, gradient. Integrations: shadcn/ui MCP for component search and examples.

sp-using-git-worktrees.name: sp-using-git-worktrees
sp-using-git-worktrees.description: Use when starting feature work that needs isolation from current workspace or before executing implementation plans - creates isolated git worktrees with smart directory selection and safety verification

sp-using-superpowers.name: sp-using-superpowers
sp-using-superpowers.description: Use when starting any conversation - establishes how to find and use skills, requiring Skill tool invocation before ANY response including clarifying questions

sp-verification-before-completion.name: sp-verification-before-completion
sp-verification-before-completion.description: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always

sp-writing-plans.name: sp-writing-plans
sp-writing-plans.description: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code

sp-writing-skills.name: sp-writing-skills
sp-writing-skills.description: Use when creating new skills, editing existing skills, or verifying skills work before deployment
